notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0086.tlg008.1st1K-gr: ἄρτια μερίζοντες, rendered 'guessing odd and even', is unusual and the exact game meant is uncertain. The line ends mid-sentence; the saying it introduces follows in the next line.

nodes.text: In general, since some of the other animals also dream, dreams would not be sent by god, nor have they come about for this purpose; they are, however, *daimonia* [of the order of spirits]: for nature is *daimonia*, but not divine. A sign of this: quite ordinary people are foresighted and have dreams that come true directly, which shows that it is not god who sends them; rather, those whose nature is, as it were, talkative and melancholic see visions of every kind; for because they are moved in many and various ways, they hit upon visions that resemble [events], being lucky in these as some are at guessing odd and even; for as it is also said,
